postings.title: AI Engineering Team Lead
postings.description:
About Dwelly

Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. Its growing network of agencies provides its AI with real-world data, continuous feedback, and control over complete workflows, making exceptional service the standard for landlords and tenants. Today, Dwelly operates more than 15,000 properties and $470 million in GMV, making it one of the UK’s ten largest lettings operators. The company has raised $263 million.

We’re a fast-growing, product-focused company, backed by top-tier investors and led by a team with deep experience in real estate, technology, and operations.

Position Summary

We are hiring exceptional engineering leaders for Tenant Find and Growth. Each leader will own an area: its technical direction, product delivery, and the organisation needed to build it.

We expect these areas to grow significantly. You will start close to the work and build towards a team of 7–10 engineers, hiring and developing the team, growing new leaders, and evolving its structure as the scope expands. We are looking for people who have operated as a CTO, Senior Engineering Manager, or in a role with comparable responsibility for building and scaling engineering teams.

You will work closely with product and operations, turn messy agency processes into reliable systems, and make decisions independently. You will remain hands-on in architecture, code reviews, debugging, and implementation where your involvement has the most impact.

Key Responsibilities

- Product outcomes: partner with product and operations on priorities, scope, and delivery. Own the path from problem definition to production and measurable business impact.

- AI products: lead the delivery of LLM and agentic workflows into production. Own quality evaluation, observability, human feedback, and safe fallbacks; measure reliability, cost, and reductions in manual work.

- AI-enabled engineering: build the team's ability to use coding agents effectively, with strong context, automated reviews, tests, and verification. Hire and develop engineers who can build and operate reliable AI systems.

- Technical direction: guide architecture, integrations, data models, and legacy migration. Balance speed with quality, reliability, and the ability to support growth.

- Hands-on engineering: stay actively involved in building the product. Write production code, design and implement complex systems, review critical changes, and lead by example. Balance hands-on contributions with growing the team and delegating ownership.

- People leadership: set clear expectations, give direct feedback, manage performance, and create an environment where people grow and raise problems early.

- Hiring and team building: define the capabilities your area needs, own hiring and onboarding, and build a strong team with high standards and shared ownership.

- Organisational growth: shape team boundaries, responsibilities, and leadership as the area scales. Develop engineers and future leaders, delegate real authority, and build teams that operate independently.

- Cross-team delivery: resolve dependencies directly with other leaders, agree shared interfaces and standards, and take responsibility for outcomes that cross team boundaries.

Qualifications and Preferred Background

- Experience as a CTO, Senior Engineering Manager, or an engineering leader with comparable scope and accountability. You have owned technical strategy, hiring, people development, and delivery through a meaningful period of growth.

- A demonstrated record of building and scaling strong engineering teams: hiring well, developing leaders, evolving organisational structure, and increasing team autonomy.

- Deep technical credibility built through designing, shipping, and operating complex production systems. You can challenge architectural decisions and still get into the code when needed.

- Strong product and business judgment: you connect engineering priorities to operational efficiency, customer experience, and business economics.

- Strong backend and systems expertise, including APIs, SQL, integrations, and legacy evolution; hands-on experience with Node.js and TypeScript.

- Experience shipping and operating LLM or agentic products in production, with evidence of business impact. You understand tool use, orchestration, evaluation, and failure modes, and can judge when to use AI, deterministic software, or human review. You actively use coding agents and can raise the team's capability.

- High autonomy and the ability to lead through ambiguity, make difficult trade-offs, and align people across teams.

What Success Looks Like

- Agencies and tenants feel the difference: work that used to take hours now happens automatically, and you can show exactly how much time and money it saves.

- Your AI workflows run reliably in production, and the people who depend on them trust them, because you’ve built in evaluations, observability, and smart fallbacks.

- Your team ships faster with coding agents than they ever could without them, and quality goes up, not down.

- You’ve built a team people want to join, grown engineers into leaders, and created teams that run independently.

- As the organisation grows, your area keeps its pace, with decisions made at the right level.

- You thrive in ambiguity, bringing clarity and making sound decisions when everything around you is moving fast.

Technology Stack

We are moving from a legacy PHP monolith toward a backend-heavy TypeScript architecture. Our stack includes Node.js, TypeScript, React, tRPC, Drizzle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. We value strong engineering fundamentals, AI-assisted development, and a short path from decision to production.

Compensation and benefits

- This is a hybrid role based in London, combining time together in the office with the flexibility of working from home.

- Competitive salary with the potential for equity options based on performance, recognising exceptional contributions to our integration success.

What is it like being a Dwell-er

Feel free to check out Dwelly Core Principles. That’s about what we believe in, how we operate and make decisions

What we offer is not a fancy office or a static workplace. Instead, this is solving one of the world’s most complex problems in the largest consumer industry in the world (residential rentals), to improve the experience for over 30% of households (more than 5 million in the UK, and over 100 million including EU and US) that live in rental homes

This is about disrupting the largest, most antiquated industry in the world, with one of the strongest operational and technical teams that exist in the UK and the EU. We work hard, and we shoot for extremely ambitious results. But we want people to be proud of what they’ve built and be able to look back and say one day “hell yeah, that was me that did it all”

postings.title: Applied AI Engineer
postings.description:
About Dwelly

Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. Its growing network of agencies provides its AI with real-world data, continuous feedback, and control over complete workflows, making exceptional service the standard for landlords and tenants. Today, Dwelly operates more than 15,000 properties and $470 million in GMV, making it one of the UK’s ten largest lettings operators. The company has raised $263 million.

We’re a fast-growing, product-focused company, backed by top-tier investors and led by a team with deep experience in real estate, technology, and operations.

Position Summary

We’re looking for an Applied AI Engineer to help build the agentic infrastructure that powers automation across Dwelly. Our growth model is acquisition. Every agency we acquire brings new operational workflows, legacy processes, and manual work. If we manage each new agency manually, the economics of the model break. Our ability to scale depends on turning complex operational processes into reliable AI-driven and automated systems.

We already have successful AI-driven flows running in Tenant Find and Property Management. They work and deliver real business results. But they were built quickly and as separate systems.

The next challenge is to bring these approaches together: build reusable agentic infrastructure, establish a robust evaluation and observability layer, and create systems that allow us to automate new workflows quickly and reliably as Dwelly scales.

This is not an AI research role. You will be building AI systems that operate inside a real business and are expected to work reliably in production.

We’re hiring remotely across the UK, Ireland, and European time zones. Candidates should be based within these regions/time zones to enable effective collaboration with the wider team.

Key Responsibilities

1. Agentic infrastructure

- Design and build the core primitives behind our agentic systems, including memory, context management, tool-calling, orchestration, and feedback loops.

- Move us from one-off AI solutions toward reusable infrastructure where new workflows can be introduced quickly and with predictable reliability.

2. Evaluation & observability

- Build the evaluation framework that allows us to understand how our agents perform and why they succeed or fail.

- Make testing, tracing, debugging, and evaluating AI systems as fundamental to our engineering process as unit testing traditional software.

- Develop the systems that allow us to confidently assess an agentic workflow before deploying it into production.

3. Agentic development

- Push forward how we use LLMs to build software itself.

- Create workflows where coding agents and specialized subagents can explore repositories, implement changes, review architecture, check conventions, run evaluations, and iterate with minimal human coordination.

- Use agentic engineering workflows extensively in your own day-to-day development.

4. Orchestration

- Design systems where specialized agents, tools, deterministic software, and humans work together effectively.

- Understand when a problem should be solved with an LLM, when traditional software is the better solution, and when multiple coordinated agents can materially improve the outcome.

5. Operational automation

- Act as the bridge between complex operational workflows and engineering.

- Work closely with our operational and product teams to understand how work actually happens across acquired agencies, identify the highest-leverage opportunities for automation, and turn them into reliable production systems.

6. Architectural influence

- Help define the architectural patterns we use for agentic systems as the company scales.

- You won’t be joining as engineer #20 on an established AI platform. You will be an early core member of the team with significant influence over our technical approach, tooling, and engineering standards.

Qualifications and Preferred Background

- 

Strong software engineering background with experience independently delivering complex systems from idea through to production

- 

Hands-on experience building AI or agentic systems that have operated in production

- 

Experience dealing with real-world AI challenges such as reliability, latency, context management, failure modes, evaluation, and observability

- 

Strong understanding of agents, tool use, structured outputs, context management, orchestration, evaluation, and feedback loops

- 

Advanced practical use of modern LLMs — not simply using ChatGPT or Claude occasionally, but understanding how to build reliable workflows around probabilistic systems

- 

Experience using coding agents and agentic development workflows as part of your own engineering process

- 

Experience decomposing complex engineering tasks across agents or specialized subagents and designing mechanisms for them to verify and improve their outputs

- 

Strong architectural judgment and ability to decide when to use LLMs, deterministic software, human intervention, or a combination of approaches

- 

Experience with TypeScript / Node.js, or strong experience building AI systems in Python with the ability and willingness to apply that knowledge in a TypeScript-first environment

- 

High autonomy, ownership, and comfort making decisions under ambiguity

- 

Strong product judgment and ability to connect technical decisions to operational and business outcomes

- 

Strong communication skills and fluency in English

- 

Startup mentality: resilience, adaptability, and ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment

What We Don't Mean by “AI Experience”

For this role, AI experience does not mean:

- 

Using ChatGPT to generate snippets of code

- 

Adding a single LLM API call to an application

- 

Building a prompt wrapper and calling it an agent

- 

Blindly accepting whatever a coding agent generates

We are looking for engineers who think in terms of agents, tools, context, orchestration, evaluation, feedback loops, and human-machine collaboration — and who already apply these concepts in their day-to-day engineering work.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

- 

Reliability: We can deploy a new agentic workflow and understand how it will perform before it reaches production because we have robust evaluation and observability systems in place.

- 

Speed: Integrating processes from newly acquired agencies takes days rather than weeks because we have a standardized library of reusable agentic primitives.

- 

Efficiency: A significant amount of repetitive operational work has been automated, allowing our teams to focus on the areas where human judgment and interaction create the most value.

- 

Engineering leverage: Agentic development workflows materially increase the speed and quality at which our engineering team can build, test, and evolve software.

Technology Stack

TypeScript (Primary) · Node.js · PostgreSQL · LLM Orchestration · Agentic Workflows

Why This Might Not Be for You

This role is probably not the right fit if:

- 

You primarily want to research new models, read the latest papers, or train custom models. We are pragmatic builders rather than an AI research lab.

- 

You prefer working from a clearly defined backlog where someone else determines what should be built.

- 

You enjoy prototyping AI systems but are less interested in the less glamorous work required to make them reliable — evaluation, logging, error handling, observability, infrastructure, and operational edge cases.

- 

You see AI primarily as a feature rather than a new way of designing and building software systems.

Compensation and benefits

- Competitive salary with the potential for equity options based on performance, recognising exceptional contributions to our integration success

This is about disrupting the largest, most antiquated industry in the world, with one of the strongest operational and technical teams that exist in the UK and the EU. postings.title: Area Director
postings.description:
Location: UK (field-based, in branches every week)

Team: Commercial, will report to UK General Manager

Package: Competitive compensation + bonus + car allowance 

About Dwelly

Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. Its growing network of agencies provides its AI with real-world data, continuous feedback, and control over complete workflows, making exceptional service the standard for landlords and tenants. Today, Dwelly operates more than 15,000 properties and $470 million in GMV, making it one of the UK’s ten largest lettings operators. The company has raised $263 million.

We’re a fast-growing, product-focused company, backed by top-tier investors and led by a team with deep experience in real estate, technology, and operations.

The role

As Area Director you lead the Client Directors of up to 10 geographically close Dwelly branches, covering 4,000 to 7,000 managed properties, and report to the UK General Manager. You own the area's growth and profit. You set a number for every Client Director, run a weekly sales cadence to hit it, and close the gap between your best and weakest branch.

You will be in branches every week, working with Client Directors, valuers and our central team, and you will integrate newly acquired agencies into your area as Dwelly grows.

What you'll own

Sales performance and cadence

- Set a number for every Client Director and run the cadence to hit it: daily pipeline check, weekly 1:1s, a weekly area pipeline call, and a monthly forecast and branch league table.

- Close the gap between your best and weakest branch, measured on lead-to-instruction conversion by branch.

Landlord relationships and key accounts

- Win and keep the big landlords: hold the key accounts and lead the negotiations, measured on revenue per property and landlord churn.

People and coaching

- Coach on the floor by joining valuations and landlord meetings, and sharpen the pitch and the fee conversation. Hire, develop and, where needed, move on Client Directors and valuers.

Commercial discipline and growth

- Keep fees, pricing and upsell consistent in every branch, and deliver on new properties signed, net portfolio growth and area EBITDA. Integrate newly acquired agencies into your area.

What you'll bring

Must have

- A record of running several branches, or a large team, at a sales-led, high-volume agency and beating targets.

- A sales cycle you have built and tracked: pipeline, forecast, conversion and a weekly rhythm.

- Experience managing managers to a number.

- Lettings knowledge, commercial judgement on fees and pricing, and P&L literacy.

- The presence to win over senior landlords and lead people who sell.

- Clear written and spoken English, and the judgment to make good decisions quickly with incomplete information.

If you meet most of the must-haves and are excited by the role, please apply. We hire for ability and trajectory, not a perfect match to a list.

Compensation and benefits

- Competitive compensation, based on your skills and experience, plus a bonus that is uncapped on new properties signed above target.

- Car allowance: included in the package.

- Ownership and progression: real ownership of an area, with the data to run it and a central team to support you, and a path to Regional Director as Dwelly grows.

- Stock options: we offer stock options, so you can share in Dwelly’s long-term growth.

- Team and culture: A closely connected international team, with regular get-togethers and company-funded social events.

How we work

We're solving one of the most complex problems in the largest consumer industry there is: residential rentals. We work hard, set ambitious goals and give people real ownership, so that you can look back and say "I built that". Our principles guide how we make decisions:

- Customer obsession rather than competitor focus

- Passion for invention

- Operational excellence

- Long-term thinking

Read more in our Dwelly Core Principles.

Our hiring process

We aim to complete the process at pace and will keep you updated at every stage.

- First interview with our Talent team (30 min)

- Hiring manager interview (45 min)

- Executive interview with Director of Launch (45 min)

- Founder interview (30 min)

- Business case: a practical exercise based on a real problem from the role (60 min)

A note on preparation

Our hiring process is comprehensive, because we’re still small enough that every person we hire shapes our culture and our results. Two stages need some preparation from you:

- Business case: a practical exercise based on a real challenge from the role. It’s the best way for you to show us how you work, not just tell us, and for you to see the problems you’d be solving.

- Founder interview: a conversation with one of our founders about your motivation, judgment and how you approach problems. Come ready to talk about your thinking, not only your CV.

We’ll share clear guidance ahead of both. Candidates who prepare well tend to enjoy these stages most.

Equal opportunities

Dwelly is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential. We value different perspectives and are committed to building a team where everyone feels respected and included.

By applying for this position, you consent to the processing and storage of your personal data for recruitment purposes for up to 365 days, in accordance with our data retention policy and applicable data protection laws.

You will own every IT project with a start and an end: bringing newly acquired agencies under group control, onboarding them to our MSP, running their digital transformation, and delivering group-wide IT rollouts.

Agency takeover

- Run IT discovery at newly acquired agencies: tenants, domains and DNS, phone lines and numbers, network and hardware, SaaS accounts and who holds the keys.

- Keep a single, current inventory of what we own and control at each agency.

- Turn takeover, supplier exit and onboarding into a repeatable playbook (checklists, templates and standard letters to outgoing suppliers), so every new agency is faster than the last.

Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. The role

As Dwelly continues to grow and prepares to move into its new five-floor London headquarters, we're hiring a Workplace Operations Manager to take ownership of our day-to-day office operations and workplace experience.

Reporting to the EA Lead, you'll be responsible for managing our self-managed office, maintaining high operational standards, overseeing facilities and suppliers, and proactively identifying opportunities for improvement. You'll have the autonomy to establish processes, introduce new initiatives and create an organised, welcoming and efficient workplace that supports our teams as Dwelly scales.

What you'll own

Workplace operations

- Own the day-to-day operations of our five-floor London HQ, ensuring workspaces, meeting rooms, kitchens and communal areas are consistently maintained to a high standard.

- Anticipate workplace requirements as the business grows, ensuring the office remains fully equipped, organised and operationally efficient.

- Act as the primary point of contact for workplace matters, proactively resolving issues and implementing sustainable solutions.

Facilities and maintenance

- Oversee building maintenance, cleaning, repairs, security and health and safety requirements, ensuring a safe and functional working environment.

- Manage external contractors and service providers, holding them accountable for quality, reliability and delivery.

- Establish scalable processes that support the effective running of our headquarters.

Supplier and budget management

- Own supplier relationships and the procurement of office equipment, refreshments and workplace essentials.

- Monitor workplace expenditure and coordinate invoice processing, maintaining visibility over operational costs.

- Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and deliver value for money without compromising the workplace experience.

Office logistics

- Ensure deliveries, post, building access and visitor arrangements are managed efficiently.

- Maintain organised, functional meeting rooms and shared spaces that support productive working.

- Support the practical logistics of employee onboarding, internal meetings and office activities.

Events and workplace experience

- Deliver team socials, office events, celebrations and internal initiatives that strengthen collaboration and team culture.

- Create a welcoming workplace that provides a positive experience for employees and visitors.

- Gather employee feedback and introduce initiatives that continuously improve the workplace experience as Dwelly scales.

What you'll bring

Must have

- Previous experience in workplace management, office management, facilities coordination or a similar workplace operations role.

- Demonstrated ability to independently manage day-to-day office operations, anticipate requirements and resolve operational challenges.

- Experience managing external suppliers, contractors and workplace expenditure.

- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining high operational standards.

- A proactive, hands-on approach to problem-solving and process improvement.

- Clear written and spoken English, and the judgment to make good decisions quickly with incomplete information.

Nice to have

- Experience working in a fast-growing technology company, startup or scale-up.

- Experience managing a multi-floor or self-managed office environment.

- Experience supporting an office relocation or establishing a new headquarters.

- Knowledge of workplace health and safety requirements.

- Experience organising employee engagement initiatives and company events.

If you meet most of the must-haves and are excited by the role, please apply. We hire for ability and trajectory, not a perfect match to a list.

Compensation and benefits

- Competitive compensation, based on your skills and experience.

- Stock options: we offer stock options, so you can share in Dwelly’s long-term growth.

- Team and culture: A closely connected international team, with regular get-togethers and company-funded social events.

How we work

We're solving one of the most complex problems in the largest consumer industry there is: residential rentals. We work hard, set ambitious goals and give people real ownership, so that you can look back and say "I built that". Our principles guide how we make decisions:

- Customer obsession rather than competitor focus

- Passion for invention

- Operational excellence

- Long-term thinking

Read more in our Dwelly Core Principles.

Our hiring process

We aim to complete the process within 2 to 4 weeks and will keep you updated at every stage.

- First interview with our Talent team (30 min)

- Hiring manager interview (30-45 min)

- Team interview with the people you'd work with every day (30-45 min)

- Founder interview (30-45 min)

- Business case: a practical exercise based on a real problem from the role (60 min)

- Offer

A note on preparation

Our hiring process is comprehensive, because we’re still small enough that every person we hire shapes our culture and our results. Two stages need some preparation from you:

- Business case: a practical exercise based on a real challenge from the role. It’s the best way for you to show us how you work, not just tell us, and for you to see the problems you’d be solving.

- Founder interview: a conversation with one of our founders about your motivation, judgment and how you approach problems. Come ready to talk about your thinking, not only your CV.

We’ll share clear guidance ahead of both. Candidates who prepare well tend to enjoy these stages most.

Equal opportunities

Dwelly is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential. We value different perspectives and are committed to building a team where everyone feels respected and included.
